chunks: 5366 - Al-Husayn ibn ʿUlwān narrated from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from ʿAlī, peace be upon him:
"He used to hold the owner of the dog liable if it bit during the day, and he would not hold him liable if it bit during the night."
And if you enter the house of a people with their permission and their dog bites you, then they are liable. But if you enter without their permission, then there is no liability upon them.

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْكَلْبِ: the owner or keeper of the dog
key_terms.يُضَمِّنُ: to hold legally liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: When is the owner of a dog liable if the dog bites someone?
ai.summary: This hadith states a fiqh ruling concerning liability for harm caused by a dog. It distinguishes between daytime and nighttime incidents, and also between entering a house with permission or without permission, making liability dependent on circumstances of access and responsibility.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5366 - Al-Husayn ibn Alwan narrated from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as):
"Imam (as) used to hold the owner of a dog liable if it bit during the day, but he would not hold him liable if it bit during the night.
And if you enter the house of people with their permission and their dog bites you, they are liable. However, if you enter without their permission, there is no liability upon them."
